def: Finding structure in data without a target to predict, so there is no label to score the result against.
A set of rows that are more similar to each other than to the rest, under a chosen distance.
A clustering method that divides rows into k groups by alternately assigning points to the nearest centre and moving each centre to its group's mean.
The total squared distance from each point to the centre of its cluster, which k-means minimises.
A seeding rule that picks each new starting centre with probability proportional to its squared distance from the existing centres.
Plotting inertia against the number of clusters and looking for the bend after which extra clusters help little.
For each point, the gap between its distance to the nearest other cluster and to its own, scaled to between -1 and +1 and averaged.
Hierarchical clustering that starts with every row as its own cluster and repeatedly merges the two closest.
A tree recording the order and height of merges in hierarchical clustering, which can be cut at any height to give a clustering.
The rule for the distance between two clusters in hierarchical clustering, such as single, complete, average or Ward.
A density-based clustering method that grows clusters from core points within a radius eps and labels unreachable points as noise.
A measure of agreement between two clusterings that is 1 for identical partitions and about 0 for chance agreement.
A way of choosing the number of clusters by comparing within-cluster dispersion with that of structureless reference data.
